newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Abu Dhabi sets up fund to develop small industry.
newsitem.headline: Abu Dhabi sets up fund to develop small industry.

text.p: Abu Dhabi's General Industry Corp has launched a 100 million dirham fund to give soft loans to small- and medium-sized industry, the fund's chief said.

"The fund will initially be 100 million dirhams. We will give loans of up to 50 percent of the project's capital or 10 percent of the fund's capital," Hamad al-Dhaheri, director of the GIC's industrial loans department, told Reuters.
He said the loans were limited to national companies in Abu Dhabi, which is trying to give the private sector a bigger role in its oil-run and state-dominated economy.
"We will target projects which create 20 percent value added, with a minimum internal rate of return of 10 percent. The project has to be high-tech and not labour intensive," he said.
The payback period for the loans is three to 10 years, with a grace period of up to three years. Annual interest of four percent is payable quarterly, Dhaheri said.
He expected most of the loans to be given to projects which involved the manufacture or assembly of electrical equipment such as integrated circuits, computers and televisions.
Government-owned GIC promotes non-oil industry in Abu Dhabi, the richest of seven members of the United Arab Emirates.
